Finally back to repairing the mini lathe. The motor bearings broke loose due to poor manufacturing and stress. I designed a more robust part for each end and printed in PETG. The PETG melted under heavy load. So now we are trying MSLA "Tough" (82A?) resin print. t.co

video

1597099356796071936.a: Gray resin is holding the motor brushes in place. The previous PETG print melted under load. Hopefully the tough resin can handle a little bit higher temp. Also, high temp resin is available if this fails. We are now at the point we just hit print and walk away to make new parts. t.co

1597100103827095553.a: Technically speaking, it would be possible to just 3D print a whole new lathe. We will be able to plate the plastic in metal for electrical connections and heat dissipation. I mean, seriously, we can print the entire motor now with only a little post-processing. That's crazy.

1597100919308840960.a: This is not even expensive or difficult. It can seriously injure you if you are not careful. Metal salts, heat, electricty, etc are not childs play. They are also no more complex than cooking. As long as you don't put bleach in the cake mix or drink the lighter fluid you're good.
